recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No follow-up is needed for FHIR-5390 unless a new work-group issue changes current binding-strength semantics.
issue_request: The Published/Persuasive with Modification ballot comment asked why isExtensible made a distinction unless conformance was Required; the accepted resolution was svn 4300, removing isExtensible and Conformance and replacing them with a single strength element, referring to FHIR-3187.
initial_application: The recorded svn 4300 application corresponds to git commit f45d3ec3d14c29dee23b1c9f5f7c4b18d99cdf7c, which added ElementDefinition.binding.strength, inactivated ElementDefinition.binding.isExtensible and ElementDefinition.binding.conformance, and introduced binding-strength terminology prose.
additional_context: FHIR-3187 records the detailed motion for the same binding-strength model. FHIR-5781 is the same ElementDefinition.binding rationalization family, and FHIR-7472 later cleaned up vestigial binding terminology. Those related decisions are already represented on the combined branch, so FHIR-5390 only needed a seed-specific audit.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Current source lists ElementDefinition as an active normative type, defines ElementDefinition.binding.strength with the BindingStrength code set, explains binding strength and additional bindings in the terminology narrative, and has no active ElementDefinition.binding.isExtensible or ElementDefinition.binding.conformance paths under source.
